acts.title: The Industry Illusion (0:00 - 1:30)
acts.speaker: selene
acts.visual_cue: Container 2: Selene portrait on 3D cyan grid. Container 3: Graph of RAM usage exploding at 128k context.
acts.script: Commercial AI providers want you to believe that a one-million token context window is an engineering triumph. What they don't tell you on their pricing pages is the brutal thermodynamic reality: standard key-value caching scales with quadratic memory consumption. At 128,000 tokens on a 70-billion parameter model, your KV cache alone eats over 30 gigabytes of high-bandwidth memory before generating a single word. Today, we are breaking that memory wall right here on bare-metal silicon, with zero cloud tokens and zero corporate hype.

acts.title: The Mathematical Dissection (1:30 - 4:45)
acts.speaker: maxx
acts.visual_cue: Container 1: Live AST memory graph. Container 3: Python memory profiler demonstrating Poincaré hyperbolic projections.
acts.script: Let's look at the math that industry tutorials conveniently skip. In Euclidean space, every token's attention key requires discrete floating-point coordinates across all heads. But human language and code aren't flat Euclidean grids; they form hierarchical trees. By projecting KV tensors into a hyperbolic Poincaré disk manifold with 3,200-byte HexCell strides, the metric tensor naturally compresses hierarchical sub-branches. We maintain the exact same attention geometry with an 82% reduction in memory footprint.

acts.title: The Adversarial Flame-Test (4:45 - 8:00)
acts.speaker: vance
acts.visual_cue: Container 2: Vance portrait with red audit overlay. Container 3: 10,000 needle-in-haystack test running in terminal at 350 tokens/sec.
acts.script: I don't care about theoretical papers. Papers don't run production systems. We put Maxx's hyperbolic HexCell compressor through ten thousand randomized needle-in-haystack needle retrievals. At 4,096 context bounds, standard retrieval degraded by 4.2% due to quantization noise. The Poincaré HexCell stride retained 99.4% precision while keeping total KV cache allocation strictly under 48 megabytes. That is the Secured Assurance mark.

acts.script: Here is what happens behind the scenes in real autonomous systems that tech influencers hide. Look at Container 1 right now: our autonomous governance daemon just detected a slight memory pressure spike on thread four. Instead of crashing or asking for a manual restart, the supervisor hot-applied a memory rebalance in 0.0004 seconds. You are watching an operating system self-heal in real time.
